title: Black Holes
tagline: From thought experiment to first image.
source: Generated from “Timeline of black hole physics” on Wikipedia; each event links to its source article.

events.title: John Wheeler
events.text: John Wheeler introduces the term "black hole" in his lecture to the American Association for the Advancement of Science

references.label: American Association for the Advancement of Science

events.title: Karl Schwarzschild
events.text: Karl Schwarzschild and independently Johannes Droste solve the Einstein vacuum field equations for uncharged spherically symmetric non-rotating systems

events.title: Maarten Schmidt
events.text: Maarten Schmidt discovers and analyzes the first quasar, 3C 273, as a highly red-shifted active galactic nucleus, a billion light years away

events.title: Paul Ehrenfest
events.text: Paul Ehrenfest gives conditional principle a three-dimensional space

events.title: Robert Oppenheimer
events.text: Robert Oppenheimer and Hartland Snyder calculate the gravitational collapse of a pressure-free homogeneous fluid sphere into a black hole

events.title: Roger Penrose
events.text: Roger Penrose discusses the Penrose process for the extraction of the spin energy from a Kerr black hole

events.title: cosmic censorship hypothesis
events.text: Roger Penrose proposes the cosmic censorship hypothesis

events.title: Roger Penrose
events.text: Roger Penrose proves that an imploding star will necessarily produce a singularity once it has formed an event horizon

events.title: Roy Kerr
events.text: Roy Kerr solves the Einstein vacuum field equations for uncharged symmetric rotating systems, deriving the Kerr metric for a rotating black hole

events.title: quantum field theory
events.text: Stephen Hawking applies quantum field theory to black hole spacetimes and shows that black holes will radiate particles with a black-body spectrum which can cause black hole evaporation

events.title: Stephen Hawking
events.text: Stephen Hawking proves that the area of a classical black hole's event horizon cannot decrease

events.title: Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar
events.text: Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar calculates, using special relativity, that a non-rotating body of electron-degenerate matter above a certain limiting mass (at 1.4 solar masses) has no stable solutions

events.title: The first recorded use of the term "black hole" in writing, by journal
events.text: The first recorded use of the term "black hole" in writing, by journalist Ann Ewing

references.label: Encyclopedia article: Timeline of black hole physics

events.title: Richard Chace Tolman
events.text: Using the work of Richard Chace Tolman, Robert Oppenheimer and George Volkoff calculate the upper mass limit of a cold, non-rotating neutron star to be approximately 0.7 solar masses.

events.title: Werner Israel
events.text: Werner Israel presents the proof of the no-hair theorem at King's College London

events.title: Yakov Zel'dovich
events.text: Yakov Zel'dovich and Igor Novikov propose searching for black hole candidates among binary systems in which one star is optically bright and X-ray dark and the other optically dark but X-ray bright (the black hole candidate)

events.title: Yakov Zel'dovich
events.text: Yakov Zel'dovich and independently Edwin Salpeter propose that accretion discs around supermassive black holes are responsible for the huge amounts of energy radiated by quasars

events.title: Max Planck Institute for Extraterrestrial Physics
events.text: Astronomers at the Max Planck Institute for Extraterrestrial Physics present evidence for the hypothesis that Sagittarius A* is a supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way galaxy.

references.label: Max Planck Institute for Extraterrestrial Physics

events.title: NASA
events.text: NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory identifies double galactic black holes system in merging galaxies NGC 6240.

events.title: The Ohio State University
events.text: Physicists at The Ohio State University publish fuzzball theory, which is a quantum description of black holes positing that they are extended objects composed of strings and don't have singularities.

events.title: UCLA
events.text: Further observations by a team from UCLA present even stronger evidence supporting Sagittarius A* as a black hole.

events.title: VLBI
events.text: One of the first VLBI observations of the black hole Sagittarius A* are made by a team that later becomes part of the Event Horizon Telescope collaboration

events.title: Suvi Gezari
events.text: First visual evidence of black-holes: Suvi Gezari's team in Johns Hopkins University, using the Hawaiian telescope Pan-STARRS 1, publish images of a supermassive black hole 2.7 million light-years away swallowing a red giant

events.title: LIGO Scientific Collaboration
events.text: LIGO Scientific Collaboration detects the distinctive gravitational waveforms from a binary black hole merging into a final black hole, yielding the basic parameters (e.g., distance, mass, and spin) of the three spinning black holes involved.

events.title: Event Horizon Telescope
events.text: Event Horizon Telescope collaboration releases the first direct photo of a black hole, the supermassive M87* at the core of the Messier 87 galaxy.

events.title: Sagittarius A*
events.text: Event Horizon Telescope releases the first image of the supermassive black hole Sagittarius A* at the centre of the milky way galaxy.
